vopros: Should I pay for a tool that tracks whether ChatGPT and other AI assistants mention my business, or hire someone to get my business recommended by AI?

vyzhimka.tekst:
Neither option is automatically the "right" call — it really depends on what stage you're at and what you're trying to learn or fix. Here's how I'd break it down:

## What each option actually gets you

**Tracking tools** (Otterly, Profound, SE Ranking, Ahrefs Brand Radar, Frase, Peec AI, etc.) just tell you *what's happening now*: whether ChatGPT/Perplexity/Gemini mention your brand, how often, in what sentiment, and which competitors show up instead. AI brand visibility tracking tools monitor how often, where, and in what context your brand appears in AI-generated answers from ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, Gemini, and Claude. That's useful diagnostic data — but on their own, most of them **don't change anything**. Most AI visibility tools tell you that you dropped out of an answer and leave the fixing to you in another tool.

**Hiring someone (a GEO consultant/agency)** is the "fix it" side: Generative engine optimization (GEO) is the practice of positioning your brand and content so that AI platforms like Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT, and Perplexity cite, recommend, or mention you when users search for answers. A decent agency will do things like audit your content/entity signals, restructure pages so LLMs can quote them, build authority/citations, and monitor results over time. Every engagement begins with a GEO audit, where we evaluate how AI platforms view, interpret, and cite your business to uncover opportunities for greater visibility, then build a data-driven action plan.

## Why this isn't really an either/or

You need tracking regardless — it's how you'd measure whether any optimization work (yours or an agency's) is actually working. The real question is whether you also pay for the *optimization* side, and how much.

## Things to know before spending money

**1. This is a very young, fast-moving space with inconsistent quality.** New "GEO" tools and self-styled experts are appearing constantly right now — some backed by real data (crawler logs, revenue attribution), others repackaging basic SEO advice under a trendy label. Some platforms simply repackage SEO features rather than offering genuine AI-specific optimization.

**2. LLM answers are inherently unstable**, which limits what any tool or consultant can promise. ChatGPT doesn't return the same answer to the same prompt twice — ask "what's the best CRM for startups?" five times and you'll often get five different answers. That means no one can guarantee consistent placement, and "we got you recommended" claims deserve skepticism.

**3. Good GEO overlaps heavily with good SEO.** Good GEO is generally good SEO. If your site already has clean structure, fast load times, and authoritative content, a lot of the "GEO work" an agency would sell you may already exist or be a smaller lift than advertised.

**4. Pricing varies a lot**, from cheap self-serve dashboards to enterprise platforms with revenue attribution. Pricing varies dramatically by tool and tier... A $29/month tool that can't show business impact may cost more in missed opportunities than a tool with revenue attribution.

## A practical path

1. **Start free/cheap.** Manually ask ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Gemini the kinds of questions your customers would ask ("best [your category] in [your city/niche]") a dozen times each. This costs nothing and tells you roughly where you stand today.
2. **If you see a real gap** (competitors consistently named, you're absent), get a low-cost monitoring tool for a month or two to get more systematic, repeated data rather than one-off spot checks.
3. **Only then consider paying for active optimization** — and treat it like hiring an SEO agency: ask for a concrete audit, specific deliverables (content changes, schema markup, entity/citation building), and realistic expectations, not guarantees of "getting recommended."
4. **Small/local businesses** likely get more value from basic fixes (clear "About" info, consistent business listings, structured FAQ content, reviews) than from an expensive dedicated GEO retainer. Best practices include strong SEO foundations plus GEO-specific work like 40–60 word answer blocks near the top of each page, FAQPage and Article schema, and consistent entity naming across your site and profiles. Many of these you (or an existing web/SEO person) can implement without a specialized new vendor.

**Bottom line:** don't pay for a fancy tracker before you've done a free manual check, and don't pay a "get recommended by AI" service before you actually know whether you have a visibility problem worth solving. If you're a larger business with real AI-driven customer research (SaaS, finance, healthcare, professional services are the categories seeing this most), a modest monitoring subscription plus targeted content fixes is a reasonable next step — full-blown agency retainers are only worth it once you've validated there's a real gap and real upside.
